tasks.short: Supervise residents and students on the ward, teach at the bedside and in sessions, fill competency assessment forms, and schedule teaching sessions.

steps.what: Hospitalist supervises medical students and residents on the ward
Hospitalist trains residents at the bedside and in teaching sessions
Hospitalist assesses the resident's competence on the task observed
Resident requests the competency assessment in the e-portfolio
Hospitalist fills competency assessment forms: on paper today, on the phone with the resident's details filled in after the change
Hospitalist schedules teaching sessions by e-mail

tasks.design: Residents request a competency assessment in their e-portfolio ({LMS}), which opens the right form on the hospitalist's phone with the resident's details filled in, so paper forms are not handed in; the hospitalist writes the assessment as today. Teaching sessions are scheduled with a shared-calendar poll ({CALENDAR}) instead of e-mail rounds. Supervising and teaching stay with the hospitalist.
tasks.previous_blocker: Assessments were filled on paper and sessions arranged by e-mail.
tasks.enabler_now: E-portfolios open assessment forms on request; calendars run polls.
tasks.still_hard: Assessments are often left until the end of a rotation.
tasks.human_edge: Knowing when a resident is ready to act alone at night.

reach.learn: Whether assessments are recorded on time.

evidence.claim: E-portfolios can open assessment forms on a trainee's request; calendars run scheduling polls.

assumptions: Boundary: from trainees on the ward to sessions scheduled; the training programme is outside.
Input contract: residents use the e-portfolio; fallback is paper.

Supervision, teaching and judging competence keep their full time. s4 keeps 85 because only the resident's details and handing in go, and the hospitalist writes the assessment; s5 keeps 40 because a calendar poll replaces e-mail rounds.
Residents request assessments (s3r) in about the time handing over a form took; their time is outside the hospitalist's savings.
research_questions: Are assessments recorded during the rotation more often?

incremental.description: No upkeep for the hospitalist: answering a request is filling the form in s4, and the training office keeps the e-portfolio.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: few residents use the e-portfolio (s4 keeps 95) and the poll still needs e-mail reminders (s5 keeps 70) (3.4); high: residents request through the e-portfolio (7.2).

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

role.altitude: The hospitalist keeps supervising and teaching trainees; paper assessments and e-mail scheduling shrink.
role.ambitious_version: A hospitalist with more time to teach.
